## Rule

**Decoded 2026-06-06 (worker-7), verified by hand on all 6 train + 1 test and by 200k truth gate.**

Count cells per color 1–9 (bg excluded). `M = max count`. **Winners** = every color tied at M
(1–3 of them in distribution). Output = `M rows × len(winners) cols`; column k = the k-th winner
**ordered by leftmost column of occurrence** in the input (all rows identical). LIVE hard caps,
mirrored in every candidate: ≤ 9 output rows (officials reach M=9: train[1] is 9×2), ≤ 3 winners.
Corpus contract (§CROP-CONTRACT, 200k): inputs **exactly 10×10**, outputs 3×1..6×3 (officials to 9×2).
§CLASS-CHECK: LIVE truth 5000/5000 ⇒ **deterministic class** — every candidate miss is a real bug.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
cnt  = [(grid == c).sum() for c in range(1, 10)]
M    = max(cnt)
wins = [c for c in range(1, 10) if cnt[c-1] == M]          # 1..3 winners
wins.sort(key=lambda c: min(np.where(grid == c)[1]))        # leftmost column order
out  = np.tile(np.array(wins), (M, 1))                      # M rows x len(wins) cols
```

## Cost analysis

**LIVE autopsy (18,184 = 18,142 mem + 42 params)**: crop [1,10,10,10] 4,000 + **two identity
Gathers (`v2=[0..9]` on axes 2,3) 8,000 — pure waste** + channel-Gather [1,9,10,10] 3,600 =
15,600 B (86%) spent producing a tensor whose every consumer is a tiny reduction. The actual
rule logic costs ~2,500.

**v6 (cost 537 = 476 mem + 61 params, exact local==profile)**: 15 nodes, opset 13.
This is v5 with the winner-sort value track narrowed to F16. The F32 leftmost score `f10`
is still computed from the free input, but `_w16` is scaled to `2^12 * 16^-j`, so columns
0..9 survive a Cast to F16 with the base-16 dominance margin intact. `f10h` [1,10] and
`fwin` [1,10] each cost 20 B; `TopK3.vals` costs 6 B instead of v5's 12 B. Full gates on
the staged copy: visible 269/269, truth 200,000/200,000, AB 200,269/200,269 byte-equal,
profile 537 (269 real inputs, `--arcgen 266`). Dominant charged tensors: eq 243; c10 40;
f10 40; canvas 27; idx3 24; f10h 20; fwin 20; idx2 16.

**v8 free-output Einsum (cost 523 = 365 mem + 158 params, exact local==profile)**:
The prompt route works against v6 but loses to the refreshed team manifest row (Aditya 497,
2026-06-19). Tail pricing: retained pre-tail logic is 191 B (`c10/f10/TopK/M/ismax/f16topk/
valmask`); free-output setup adds `idxsent` 24 + F16 `khot[1,3,10]` 60 + `rows[1,30]` 30 +
F16 `rowh[1,30]` 60 = 174 B, total memory 365. Params rise to 158 from the operand tax:
`_cols[3,30]` 90 + `_iota30f[1,30]` 30 + `_w16[30]` 30 + small scalars/OneHot values 8.
The final `[1,10,30,30]` F16 output is scorer-free, and gate-5 confirms no runtime reprice
(`profile_real_cost.py --task 247 --cand ... --arcgen 266` => profile 523).

**v9 Resize tail (cost 494 = 443 mem + 51 params, exact local==profile)**:
Keeps the v6/v8 count, leftmost, and TopK winner extraction, but replaces the v8 free-output
Einsum tail. Empty TopK slots are sentinel color 10, `OneHot(axis=1)` builds a duplicated
winner strip `[1,10,2,3]`, and the final `Resize(tf_crop_and_resize, nearest/floor)` is the graph
output. For the 2-row source, `roi_h_end = 30 / M` makes exactly the first M rows map in-bounds;
the rest extrapolate to zero. `roi_w_end = 14.5` similarly keeps only columns 0..2. This removes
the v8 `_cols[3,30]` 90-param basis, `_iota30f` 30-param row basis, and `rowh[1,30]` 60 B cast,
while paying `strip` 120 B, `idxsent_2row` 48 B, `idxsent_row` 24 B, `roi` 32 B, and `roi_h_end`
4 B. Full staged gates: visible 269/269, truth 200,000/200,000, AB 200,269/200,269 byte-equal,
profile 494 (`--arcgen 262`, 269 real inputs). A U8 free-output Einsum tail was probed and
rejected: ORT has no UINT8 Einsum CPU implementation. A 1-row Resize source was also rejected:
degenerate height maps every output row in-bounds and cannot crop to M rows.

**v5 (cost 543 = 482 mem + 61 params, exact local==Kaggle per §39 static)**: 14 nodes, opset 13.
v5 = v4 with the tail rebuilt as **Equal-assembly** (task398-v4 pattern): instead of one-hot
`Equal(iota, idx)` [1,9,1,3] + `And(valmask)` [1,9,1,3] (54 B), build a u8 color-code canvas —
`code = Cast(idx3→u8)` [1,3] 3 + `codem = Where(valmask, code, 0)` [1,3] 3 +
`canvas = Where(rows, codem, 0)` [1,1,9,3] 27 — and expand channels with ONE
`Equal(canvas, chids 1..9)` → [1,9,9,3] BOOL (the pre-Pad content). −21 mem +1 param = −20.
`Equal(u8,u8)` @ opset 13 re-confirmed through the full scorer+200k path (`ort_reality.md:32`).

v4 = v3 plus the **bg-dominance lemma**, which deletes both ch0-drop Slices:
> M ≤ 9 on every valid input (officials reach 9; LIVE caps output at 9 rows and holds hidden)
> ⇒ nonbg ≤ 9 colors × 9 = 81 ⇒ **bg ≥ 19 > M**. Hence (a) bg is always the strict global
> count max ⇒ `TopK(c10, k=2)` puts bg in slot 0 and `M = vals2[:,1]`; (b) `Equal(c10, M)`
> can never fire on ch0; (c) the one-hot iota runs 1..9 so idx 0 couldn't paint anyway
> (belt+braces). All-zero scorer dummy: vals2=[0,0] ⇒ M=0 ⇒ rows all-false ⇒ output zeros.

v3/v4 shared architecture:
- Stats straight off the FREE input (`input` is scorer-skipped): counts `Einsum('bchw->bc')`
  [1,10] 40 B (equation is an attribute — beats ReduceSum's axes-input by 2p at opset 13);
  zero-padding outside the active grid makes full-canvas stats equal cropped stats.
- **Leftmost ordering without ArgMax/occupancy plane**: `f = Einsum('bchw,w->bc', input, 16^-j)`
  40 B + 30p. Base-16 positional dominance: `leftmost(c) < leftmost(d) ⇔ f(c) > f(d)`.
  Margin proof: per-column count ≤ 10 (inputs exactly 10×10) ⇒ for L_c ≤ L_d − 1:
  `f(d) < 10·16^-(L_d)·16/15 = 0.667·16^-L_c·16^(L_c−L_d+1) ≤ 0.667·16^-L_c ≤ 0.667·f(c)` —
  a 1.5× exact-arithmetic gap vs ~1e-5 F32 rounding; weights 2^(−4j) ≥ 2^−116 all normal-range.
  Replaces colocc [1,10,1,30] 1,200 + ArgMax 80 + slice/transpose/pairwise-rank (~1,800 total in v2 terms).
- **TopK(fwin, k=3 static init)** sorts winners by f desc = leftmost asc; the 3 slots ARE LIVE's
  ranks 0/1/2. Losers Where-masked to 0; empty slots (vals==0) Greater-masked. task054 precedent:
  TopK static-k scores fine.
- All-BOOL tail: Equal(iota9,idx)→And(valmask)→And(rows iota<M) → gate [1,9,9,3] BOOL 243 →
  `Pad(BOOL)` (opset 13) → BOOL graph output (decoder thresholds >0; scorer skips `output`).
- v5 tensors: c10 40, f10 40, vals2 8, idx2 16 (unconsumed TopK output — still counted),
  m 4, ismax 10, fwin 40, vals3 12, idx3 24, valmask 3, rows 9, code 3, codem 3, canvas 27,
  eq 243 = **482 mem**. Params: w16 30, _one 1, _k2 1, _k3 1, _zero 1, _zerou8 1, chids 9,
  iota9f 9, pads 8 = **61**.
  (v4 paid a one-hot tail: oneh 27 + col3 27 instead of code/codem/canvas 33 → 503+60 = 563;
  v3 additionally paid f/c ch0-Slices 72+_ten → 606.)

## Generator-source certification (2026-06-06, `external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_a3325580.py`)

Upgrades every v4 distribution bet to a certainty (lessons 2026-06-06 #6 methodology):
- `size=10` hardcoded; `common.grid(size, size)` ⇒ **inputs exactly 10×10** ⇒ per-column count
  ≤ 10 ⇒ base-16 dominance margin certain.
- `max_count = randint(3, 6)` for generated pairs; officials (validate()) hand-pass up to 9
  (train[1] idxs: 9+6+9) ⇒ **M ≤ 6 hidden-generated / ≤ 9 officials** — the 9-row cap is exact.
- Winners are EXACTLY the `num_max ∈ [1,3]` "max boxes" (each gets `max_count` cells via
  `continuous_creature`; min boxes get `xcounts ≤ max_count−1`) ⇒ **#winners ∈ [1,3], always
  ALL tied** ⇒ the k=3 cap is exact, and a "4-winner hidden input" cannot exist.
- nonbg ≤ 3·6 + 3·5 = 33 generated (≤ 51 officials) ⇒ **bg ≥ 67 (≥ 49) ≫ M** — the
  bg-dominance lemma holds with ~7× margin, not just the 19>9 worst-case bound.
- `overlaps_1d(bcols, wides)` forces the max boxes **column-disjoint**; output order is
  `sorted(bcols)` ⇒ leftmost-PIXEL order (what v3/v4 compute) ≡ box-left order (what the
  generator emits), and **leftmost ties among winners are IMPOSSIBLE** — the tie-divergence
  caveat below is formally vacuous on the real distribution.
- `random_colors(num_max+num_min)` = distinct colors per box ⇒ per-color counts ≡ per-box
  counts (no accidental merging).

**Empirical re-verification (200,000-pair vectorized scan, 2026-06-06, 0 violations)**:
`min(bg − M) = 61` (matches the source bound exactly: bg ≥ 67, M ≤ 6); min winner
leftmost-gap = 1 (ties never occur); M ∈ [3,6]; winners ≤ 3. The v5 lemmas are
triple-certified: generator-source read + 200k empirical scan + 200,269 ab byte-equality.

## Floor status / proof obligations (2026-06-22)

**No current floor claim.** The previous 543 proof is superseded: it assumed the winner-sort
TopK value track effectively stayed F32, but ORT accepts F16 TopK values and scaled base-16
leftmost weights preserve the ordering over this generator. v6 lowered the measured static and
profile cost to 537, v8 lowered the tail to 523 but lost to Aditya 497, and v9 lowers the exact
staged profile to **494**. U8/I8 TopK remains rejected by ORT (`ort_reality.md` TopK row), so the
value floor for this exact TopK stage is F16, not U8/I8.

The hostile enumeration below remains useful as historical accounting for the v5 formulation,
but its 543 conclusion is retracted. Any renewed floor proof must price the F16 winner-sort
track and must either beat or prove irreducible the current v9 charged tensors: `strip` 120,
INT64 winner-index transport 120, `c10/f10` 80, `roi`/`roi_h_end` 36, F16 `f10h/fwin/vals3`
46, `idx2` 16, `ismax`/`valmask` 13, and params 51.

## Historical v5 floor proof (superseded)

Irreducible stages under this scorer (binary ops, no select+compare fusion exists):
1. **Content tensor**: the answer pre-pad is 9ch×9row×3col; the only free big tensor is `output`
   itself, reachable only through the final node. Final-`Pad` ⇒ a [1,9,9,3] BOOL ≥ 243 B must
   materialize. Alternative final-op families priced: broadcast-`And`/`Where` final (operands
   must carry the 30-extents: ≥ 330 = **+87 worse**); OneHot-op assembly [1,3,10]+transpose =
   **+93**; full u8 canvas [1,1,30,30]+Equal ≥ 900; Conv/MatMul planes ≥ 900.
   **Tail-representation lesson (the 563→543 fall)**: feeding that 243-B Equal from a u8
   color-CODE canvas [1,1,9,3] (27 B; 3 u8 cells/column) is cheaper than feeding an And-chain
   from a one-hot [1,9,1,3] block (54 B) — code+codem+canvas = 33 B replaces oneh+col3 = 54 B.
   Code-representation beats one-hot whenever channel-expansion can ride the final pre-Pad op.
2. **Stats** (v4, slice-free via bg-dominance lemma): two free-input reductions pay only outputs
   2×40 ([1,10] F32); M-extraction = TopK(c10,2)+Gather = 28 (8 vals + 16 dead-but-counted idx
   + 4 m) — enumerated alternatives: Slice+ReduceMax 40, Gather(iota)+ReduceMax rank-5 40,
   masked-Sub ≥ 40+10p; ismax 10 + fwin 40 (Where; Mul+Cast costs +36). = 158.
3. **Select+tail**: TopK3 block 39 (vals 12 + idx 24 + mask 3) + code/codem/canvas 33 + rows 9
   = 81. Pairwise-rank alternative: **1,115 total** (the BOOL→F32 Cast 324 dominates — ORT
   ReduceSum/Einsum accept no BOOL/U8). Combined-key single TopK (c·K + f): **breaks** —
   F32 mantissa can't hold count-scale + 16^-9 discrimination simultaneously. One-hot tail
   (v4): +20. And(rows,valmask)-first canvas ordering: +24.
4. **Params**: w16 30 forced ([30] element count regardless of zeros; Range-generated iota is
   CHARGED as intermediate — 240 B > 30p, lessons 2026-06-06 #12); chids 9 + iota9f 9 (shapes/
   dtypes differ, sharing via Reshape/Transpose costs ≥ 72 B > 9p); pads 8; k2/k3/one/zero/zerou8
   5. = 61.
Historical Σ = 243 + 158 + 81 + 61 = **543** for v5, but **not a floor** after v6. Epistemic
note per lessons #10/#14: the prior "563 floor" fell to a tail-representation class (one-hot
→ u8 code), and the 543 proof fell to the F16 TopK value-track class. Remaining slack candidates
examined and dead for this session: TopK value-only / empty-index output (checker rejects; TopK
requires exactly 2 outputs), U8 non-bg M extraction (539, worse than v6), sentinel-idx Where
fusion (−2 B, +1 node), [1,10]-iota gate (+28), Pad-18 axes form (+1p).

## Don't-do log

- **Don't pre-crop the input** (crop10x10 heritage): stats off the free input cost the same and
  remove the 4,000 B crop. The two identity Gathers in LIVE were dead weight all along.
- **Don't compute counts and dominance in ONE Einsum** (`w = 1 + 16^-j`): count-scale (≤100)
  swamps f-resolution (16^-9 ≈ 4e-11) in F32 — right-side columns become indistinguishable.
- **Don't TopK an unmasked combined key** (count-primary, f-secondary): same mantissa problem.
- **The whole combined-key class is information-theoretically dead in F32** (closed 2026-06-06
  ping-1 re-sweep): one scalar holding count-order (≤100 ⇒ ~7 bits) above 10-column exponential
  leftmost-order (4 bits/column × 10) needs ~47 mantissa bits > F32's 24. A single
  `Einsum('bchw,w->bc', 16 + 16^-j)` loses all columns j ≥ 3 to rounding; rescaling only moves
  the cliff (j ≥ 4). F64 Einsum would need a 72,000 B input Cast. The Where-mask (zeroing
  losers) is precisely what keeps the two orders in SEPARATE comparisons — keep it.
- **Don't drop `valmask` hoping empty TopK slots self-mask**: ORT TopK breaks value-ties by
  LOWER index first, so with |winners|=1 the second empty slot lands on the lowest-index
  loser COLOR (not bg) and would paint a wrong column. Only slot-after-bg is safe; valmask (3 B)
  is required. (Bit-packed BitwiseAnd output expansion also enumerated: 9 active channels > 8
  u8 bits, u16 unconfirmed on CPU, u32 quadruples the inter tensor — class dead.)
- **Don't sort raw f without the ismax mask**: a loser left of a winner steals a TopK slot and
  the mask-after-sort drops a real winner.
- **#112 bit-pack + MaxPool SELECT-BY-POSITION priced DEAD vs 494** (worker w6, beta_p29, 2026-06-24,
  10-min fast-fail, no build). The prompt route (pack `pos<<k | color`, MaxPool picks largest-position
  token, mask off color) selects exactly ONE winner per pooling window. task247 emits the ORDERED set of
  up-to-3 winners simultaneously (then tiled M×K). Getting 3 ordered winners from MaxPool needs 3
  masked/iterative MaxPools = the "general sort pipeline for a small fixed winner set" the prompt
  explicitly forbids — and each masked-MaxPool stage costs ≥ the single `TopK(fwin,k3)` (vals3 6 + idx3
  24 = 30 B) v9 already pays. Bit-pack additionally forces opset 13→18 (`BitwiseOr/And` are opset-18 only,
  ort_reality §97/§646) + a charged position-coordinate plane, with the TopK still required. The base-16
  Einsum leftmost-dominance order (architecture §3/§4) is already a sort-FREE, free-INPUT select that costs
  the same/less than a packed MaxPool. Finally the DOMINANT cost is the tail (`strip` [1,10,2,3] F16 120 +
  INT64 index transport ~72 + OneHot), which is the 10-channel one-hot EXPANSION floor — independent of how
  winners are ordered, so packing the winner-sort touches none of it. (The output-EXPANSION bit-pack variant
  was already dead: 9 active channels > 8 u8 bits, u32 quadruples — see valmask note above.) No candidate;
  494 unbeaten by this family.
- **Don't replace the rank/TopK stage with ReduceSum-of-BOOL**: ORT CPU ReduceSum accepts
  float/double/int32/int64 only — the Cast to F32/I32 costs 324 B ([1,9,9,1]·4); U8 reduce is
  not registered.
- **Don't shrink the 9-row output cap to corpus max 6**: officials contain M=9 (train[1] 9×2);
  officials ⊆ hidden (§VISIBLE-FAIL axiom) ⇒ certain 0.
- **Don't reach for sparse inits** (w16 zeros): scorer rejects at 3 gates (core.md, task337 Lemma 4).
- **Ignore the `kmmmvs_local_best` "cost 110" external** (task_state `best_ext_cost`): it is a
  single 1×1 Conv channel-mixer — pointwise ops cannot localize/resize the output region, so it
  cannot implement this rule, and `score_network_v2` returns **None** on it regardless (same
  mispriced-external pattern as task228's 6 KB/798k kmmmvs mover). Not a floor counter-example.
- **Tie semantics caveat** (only known v3-vs-LIVE divergence class): two winners sharing a
  leftmost column — LIVE assigns both the same rank (emits a duplicated/multi-hot column);
  v3 orders them by deeper column profile. **Zero such inputs in 200,269 officials+corpus**
  (ab divergences=0); rotate-adversarial's 693/807 is exactly this class on off-contract inputs.
  If a future rebuild must reproduce LIVE byte-for-byte off-contract too, use v2 (ArgMax route).
